title: Progressive taxation

match.reason: The closest bank points only cover progressive tax as one part of a broader card (tax types and revenue sources, or four ways to reduce inequality), and neither teaches the narrowing of the income gap as a single focused idea, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Progressive taxation
card: A tax rate is the share of income paid as tax. A progressive tax takes a larger share of income as income rises.
Australia's income tax works this way. Income is split into bands, and each higher band is taxed at a higher rate.
A person on a high income pays more dollars in tax and also a bigger share of their income than a person on a low income.
This narrows the gap between high and low incomes, because people on high incomes keep a smaller share of each extra dollar they earn.
draft.remember: Progressive tax: the more you earn, the bigger the share you pay.

opts: A tax rate that rises as a person's income rises
A tax of the same share of income for every person
A tax of the same dollar amount for every person
A tax rate that falls as a person's income rises
a.why: A progressive tax takes a larger share of income as income rises. A same share for everyone is a flat rate, and a same dollar amount takes a bigger share from people on low incomes.
a.clue: Look at what happens to the share, not just the dollars.

b.q: Ava earns $40,000 and pays $4,000 in tax. Ben earns $120,000 and pays $24,000. Why is this tax progressive?
opts: Ben pays a larger share of his income than Ava
Ben pays more dollars in tax than Ava
Ava and Ben both pay some tax
Ben earns more money than Ava does
b.why: Ava pays 10% of her income and Ben pays 20%, so the share rises with income. Ben paying more dollars is not enough: a flat tax of 10% would also take $12,000 from him, and it would not be progressive.
b.clue: Work out each person's tax as a share of their income.

a.best: A tax rate that rises as a person's income rises

b.best: Ben pays a larger share of his income than Ava
